claims.text: The local source slice models one Pokemon Card Fan Club Vol. 3 row: Dark Persian row 024.

The selected Pokumon snapshot says Pokemon Card Fan Club Vol. 3 was released on November 18, 1997 and included an exclusive non-holo Dark Persian promotion card with different artwork than the Team Rocket/Rocket Gang copy.
Bulbapedia says the unnumbered promotional print with different Ken Sugimori artwork was available as an insert with the third volume of Pokemon Card Fan Club, released on November 18, 1997.
Bulbapedia separates the ordinary Rocket Gang/Team Rocket print credited to Shin-ichi Yoshida from the unnumbered promotional print credited to Ken Sugimori.
Bulbapedia notes that the Japanese unnumbered promotional print features the Rocket Gang symbol, indicating that it is a promotional addition to the expansion.

This release matters because it shows Pokemon Card Fan Club acting as collector infrastructure: a magazine issue was not merely talking about Team Rocket, it carried a route-specific Dark Persian object into readers' hands.

Agents should preserve Pokemon Card Fan Club Vol. 3 route, November 18 1997 timing, row 024 identity, Ken Sugimori promo artwork, Rocket Gang symbol promotional-addition context, and non-equivalence with Rocket Gang/Team Rocket, Wizards Black Star, Nintendo Power, Legendary Collection, and TCG GB2 memories before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: Pokemon Card Fan Club Vol. 3 — Dark Persian slips out before the Rocket crowd arrives
narrative.why_it_matters: Dark Persian is easy to misremember as a Team Rocket card because that is where the character energy lives. The Fan Club Vol. 3 promo is more interesting than that shortcut. It sits in the apparatus around the cards: Pokemon Card Fan Club magazine, a November 1997 reader object, and a Ken Sugimori Giovanni image that distinguishes the promo from Shin-ichi Yoshida's ordinary Rocket Gang line. The promo arrives just ahead of Rocket Gang's November 21, 1997 expansion context in the local source notes, so it feels like a magazine-doorway into the Rocket era. This is the kind of release that makes the catalog useful to agents: the name is not enough, the villain theme is not enough, and even the Rocket Gang symbol is not enough unless the route survives.

claims.text: The local catalog anchors Dark Persian as row jp_promo_fan_club_vol3_19971118:024 in the Pokemon Card Fan Club Vol. 3 Dark Persian source slice.
Bulbapedia identifies Dark Persian's Japanese name as わるいペルシアン and gives Bad Persian as the romanized/translated name.
The Fan Club Vol. 3 unnumbered promotional print is credited to Ken Sugimori, while the Rocket Gang/Team Rocket print is credited to Shin-ichi Yoshida.
Bulbapedia says the unnumbered promotional print features Giovanni in the illustration.
The selected Pokumon snapshot describes this Fan Club Vol. 3 card as an exclusive non-holo Dark Persian with different artwork than the newly released Team Rocket expansion copy.

Bulbapedia's release information connects the same Ken Sugimori artwork lineage to later Wizards Black Star / Nintendo Power distribution, while also noting that unknown quantities of the Nintendo Power print were erroneously printed without HP.

Dark Persian is a strong agent test because the name, Rocket theme, and symbol can all point in the right emotional direction while still landing on the wrong route unless the magazine-insert provenance is preserved.

Before accepting a match, require Fan Club Vol. 3 magazine route, row 024 identity, Ken Sugimori/Giovanni artwork, Rocket Gang symbol promotional-addition context, and separation from Rocket Gang, Team Rocket, Wizards Black Star, Nintendo Power, Legendary Collection, and TCG GB2 prints.

narrative.human_title: Dark Persian — Giovanni's shadow in a Fan Club magazine
narrative.why_it_matters: Dark Persian is deliciously slippery. It belongs emotionally to Team Rocket, mechanically to the Dark Pokemon era, and visually to Giovanni's orbit. But this Fan Club Vol. 3 copy is its own thing: an unnumbered Japanese promo carried by a magazine, credited to Ken Sugimori, and distinct from the Shin-ichi Yoshida Rocket Gang card. The Rocket Gang symbol is part of the identity, but not a license to collapse it into an ordinary Rocket Gang pack card. For an agent, it is a lesson in not letting theme become provenance. The card wants you to recognize the cat, the boss, and the Rocket symbol, then still ask: which route put this exact object into the world?
